vocalRests.title: Complete Vocal Rest Days
vocalRests.description: Schedule 1-2 days per week where you minimize speaking. Communicate through writing when possible. This gives your vocal folds complete recovery time.

vocalRests.title: Quiet Hours
vocalRests.description: Designate quiet hours daily (ideally 2 hours) where you speak minimally. Many performers use early mornings or late evenings for this.

vocalRests.title: Post-Performance Rest
vocalRests.description: After performances, give yourself at least 12-24 hours of minimal speaking. Avoid parties and late-night socializing. Let your voice recover.

vocalRests.title: Hydration Before Rest
vocalRests.description: Drink plenty of water before resting your voice. Well-hydrated vocal folds heal faster and remain more flexible.

vocalRests.title: Avoid Irritants During Rest
vocalRests.description: During rest periods, avoid alcohol, caffeine, smoke, and dry environments. These dehydrate your vocal folds and slow recovery.

warmups.title: Lip Trills (Bubbles)
warmups.description: Make a motorboat sound with your lips while sliding through your range. This loosens tension and increases blood flow to vocal folds. Start at your lowest note and slide to your highest.

warmups.title: Sirens
warmups.description: Make a 'ng' sound while sliding your pitch up and down, like a siren. This coordinates breathing with pitch movement and gently stretches your range.

warmups.title: Five-Tone Scale
warmups.description: Sing 'do-re-mi-re-do' on a comfortable pitch. Repeat on different syllables like 'ma,' 'me,' 'mo,' 'mu.' This builds vocal agility and warms up your range.

warmups.title: Octave Jumps
warmups.description: Sing a low note, then jump up an octave, then back down. Use an 'ng' or 'ng-ah' sound. This strengthens coordination between your registers.

warmups.title: Straw Phonation
warmups.description: Sing through a thin straw into water, creating bubbles. This creates back pressure that strengthens vocal folds and improves resonance. Very effective!

warmups.title: Arpeggio Slides
warmups.description: Sing smooth, connected arpeggios (1-3-5-3-1) using 'ng' or 'oh.' This improves legit and helps blend your registers smoothly.

warmups.title: Jaw Release
warmups.description: Drop your jaw loosely, make a 'hah' sound as if yawning. Gently massage your jaw while humming. This releases jaw tension that restricts singing.

warmups.title: Neck Rolls & Shoulder Rolls
warmups.description: Slowly roll your neck and shoulders to release tension. Tension in your neck, shoulders, and jaw reduces vocal freedom and quality.
